messages:
maya: Quick check-in on post-launch sequencing. We have a ~10-item pile with mixed severity. Need to decide: immediate patch train (2w) for high-impact bugs vs a follow-on polish wave. I sketched a proposal in the sheet: https://tiny.redwood/backlog - can we lock rules + owners?

ajay: yes. suggest deterministic rules: "urgent" vs "next-wave" driven by user-impact and regression flag. No fuzzy debates.

courtney: Draft rules: 
- urgent = data loss, crashing flow, or single-customer block -> hotpatch
- high = major UX break for core journey (>1% DAU) or billing/consistency -> hotpatch if regression or active customer
- medium = performance degradation or partial failures -> next-wave sprint
- low = polish / requests -> backlog
courtney: Also require a clear acceptance metric for any next-wave enhancement (SLO or explicit UX example).

ben: if it's a regression from last release bump severity by one. Also add a "safety owner" for DB-affecting fixes.

sara: I'll own rollout + smoke tests for the hotpatch train. Plan: small canaries, automated smoke, 30-min observation window, then roll to region. Every PR must include smoke script output.

oliver: For enhancements, split into "rapid" (<=3 dev days) and "invest" (>3 dev days). Rapid go into next sprint, invest gets a 3-day spike and a decision gate.

dena: Customer commitments: three enterprise customers reported impact. We should notify them of timeline if we schedule a hotpatch this week. Can Product send an ETA note?

maya: Yes. I'll draft a short ETA template. Decision: lock a 2-week urgent patch train starting Monday for tickets marked hotpatch. Owners: ajay (cache/profile fixes), ben (search/paging bug), sara (db edge-case), dena to lead customer comms. Remaining items labeled next-wave -> owners courtney + oliver.

ajay: Requesting a canary window Thu AM. @release-bot can you reserve and add the `hotpatch/canary` label requirement?

release-bot: Canary window reserved: 2026-05-06 09:00-10:00 UTC for team product-hotpatch. Please label PRs with `hotpatch/canary` and attach smoke logs.

ben: I'll prepare rollback steps per ticket and a runbook snippet for SRE. Will post in the ticket.

courtney: For next-wave enhancements I'll add acceptance criteria: metric, UX screenshot, and max scope sentence. Keeps PRs reviewable.

maya: Action items: 1) Owners update ticket with owner + estimate + rollout plan by EOD. 2) Dena will send ETA to affected customers once owners confirm timelines. 3) Sara to provide smoke script template. We'll reconvene Fri to confirm patches ready for canary. :thumbsup:
